Enum Class ArchitectureConfig.MemoryModelType

java.lang.Object
java.lang.Enum<ArchitectureConfig.MemoryModelType>
hu.bme.mit.theta.frontend.transformation.ArchitectureConfig.MemoryModelType
All Implemented Interfaces:

Enclosing class:
ArchitectureConfig
public static enum ArchitectureConfig.MemoryModelType extends Enum<ArchitectureConfig.MemoryModelType>
How a pointer value that lives in a memory cell is represented.
  • multi: the default 2-D model. Memory is __arrays[base][offset]; a pointer is a (base, offset) pair. Storing a pointer into a cell therefore needs the cell duplicated -- one storage location for the base, a parallel one for the offset (a struct pointer field is duplicated the same way).
  • flat: a single flat address space, as if every object's base were 0. Each object occupies a disjoint slice of one address line, so a pointer is a single scalar address (base + offset folded together) and storing it into a cell needs no duplication at all.
  • bytes: the flat address line above, but byte-granular -- every memory cell is one byte (Bv8) and a wider scalar is the Concat of its bytes on read and the Extract-and-split of them on write. Offsets are therefore real byte offsets, so two differently-typed views of the same storage (an int and the chars overlapping it, a union member and its byte array) alias correctly through the one byte array. Builds on flat addressing (a pointer must be a single scalar to be storable as bytes); requires bitvector arithmetic (byte splitting is a bitvector operation).
